svg.title: CV Protocol v5 — the reveal and the decision
svg.desc: What must be frozen and checksummed before protected truth is opened, what the reveal reports, and how Accept, Hold and Reject are decided. Public leaderboard feedback is monitoring evidence only, and the frozen parent changes only on explicit user approval.
svg.text: 05 · The reveal and the promotion decision
Everything is frozen and hashed first. Held-out labels then open once, for all five folds and several families together.
Frozen before the reveal
Each item, and what leaving it unfrozen would permit.
the selector, its variants, tie-break and seeds
otherwise: choose the rule after seeing which variant won
snapshot grid, decoder, postprocessor, weight rule
otherwise: re-sweep the 225 cheap axes against protected truth
run goal, readiness and confirmation results, heuristics
otherwise: rewrite the development story to fit the outcome
the 10 pair runs mapped to 20 roles, 5 outer checkpoints,
masked prediction caches, target-free deployment logic
otherwise: substitute a checkpoint or regenerate a prediction after the fact
source, config, checkpoint and prediction manifests
otherwise: every substitution above becomes undetectable
a ledger entry authorising this reveal
otherwise: the reveal is spent without counting, and the budget is fiction
Source and preregistration are committed first.
The sealed run may then use F4 labels for other outer contexts.
What the reveal reports
Candidate against the parent frozen before this reveal, on identical
folds, rows, masks and RMSE definition. candidate_rmse is the
gain = previous_best_rmse − candidate_rmse

g.text: resulting solution, parent with candidate blended in.
pooled and per-fold RMSE — all five folds
weight stability — positive inner weights, legacy level 10
F4 behaviour — reported separately as the audit fold
paired bootstrap — 2,000 draws over whole groups, seed 20260725

svg.text: C016's audit, as an example

g.text: 4 positive inner weights — below the legacy level of 10

svg.text: The boundary
Revision 14 made the old numeric levels diagnostics rather than gates.
Accept
the F4 gain is strictly positive, pooled selection-clean CV beats
the frozen previous best, every integrity rule passes, and
protected evidence shows no material overfitting or reversal
Hold
gain is positive but uncertainty or instability is substantial
Reject
F4 gain not positive, pooled gain not positive, or integrity fails
Only Accept may be packaged. An F4 regression is never accepted,
however small: the F4 gain must be strictly positive.
Hold and Reject end the run. The spent audit may not be re-queried,
and the failed candidate may not be tuned against it.
After the decision — the leaderboard is monitoring, not a gate
may inform
whether CV and LB move together
whether to approve a new parent
whether a validation review is due
may never inform
model or checkpoint choice
blend weights or offsets
postprocessing decisions
the parent moves only by hand
Promotion does not move it. Submission
does not move it. Only explicit user
approval after a CV–LB review does.
How a run ends
Repeated CV-up / LB-down results trigger a validation review. That is the only place the protocol looks at the leaderboard for a signal about itself —
not to tune a model, but to ask whether the validation design has started to drift.
Rules from CV_PROTOCOL_V5.md and COOKBOOK.md revision 14 · C016 figures from runs/v5_batch2_run_025_goal_050/kaggle_production/package_validation.json
